items.title: FIFA faces investigation over World Cup's 'impossibly high' ticket prices
items.description: In a joint statement, New Jersey's attorney-general accused the football governing body of having turned "buying a ticket to the World Cup into a gauntlet of confusion, fake scarcity, and impossibly high prices".

items.title: UK spy chief says West between peace and war, as Russia ramps up cyberattacks
items.description: The head of a major UK intelligence agency is warning that Moscow and other adversaries could use artificial intelligence and other emerging technology to conduct "hybrid warfare" against western allies.

items.title: White House calls leaked Iran draft deal a 'fabrication'

featured_image.name: Hormuz Flows May Return to Normal Within Month of Deal: Iran TV

items.description: Iranian state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an "initial, unofficial" framework for a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran that would restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels within one month of finalization. The White House quickly pushed back, calling the Iranian report a "total fabrication".[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says US 'not satisfied' with Iran peace deal proposals
items.description: It comes as the White House rejects a draft deal being reported by Iranian state TV as a "fabrication".

items.title: Iran state TV says it obtained draft MOU framework with US

featured_image.name: Iran's internet blackout partially lifted after 87 days

items.description: Iran's state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an initial unofficial framework for a Memorandum of Understanding with the United States, according to Reuters. The development marks the latest step in weeks of intensive diplomacy aimed at ending the conflict between Washington and Tehran that began in late February.[1]

items.title: Kalyn Ponga's Origin send-off leaves Queensland legend 'in shock'
items.description: Maroons great Darren Lockyer says the decision to send off Kalyn Ponga late in State of Origin will be hard to accept for Queenslanders.

items.title: North Korea claims first use of AI in missile tests

featured_image.name: North Korea leader Kim supervised missile test of new guidance system: KCNA

items.description: North Korea on Wednesday announced it had tested a range of advanced weapons systems, including cruise missiles guided by artificial intelligence, marking the first time Pyongyang has publicly claimed to incorporate AI into its missile technology. Leader Kim Jong Un supervised the tests on Tuesday, state media KCNA reported.[1][2][3]

items.title: Video shows divers finding five Lao cavers alive, two remain missing
items.description: A rescue mission has been underway for more than a week to find seven people who entered a cave in central Laos before becoming trapped in a landslide triggered by heavy rain.

items.title: PM response to truth-telling process 'hugely significant'
items.description: The Walk for Truth ended at Parliament House today and while there was not a firm commitment from the PM, many felt the response was a 'positive move'.

items.title: Labor MP defends electoral registration to empty block amid rebuild
items.description: Dickson MP Ali France has been referred to the Australian Electoral Commission with claims she is registered to vote at a vacant suburban block in her north Brisbane electorate.

items.title: ISIS-linked woman barred from Australia tried to board flight
items.description: An Australian woman with links to ISIS, who is barred from Australia on a temporary exclusion order, tried to board a flight home with the other members of Tuesday's returning cohort, a Senate estimates hearing has been told.

items.title: Bondi shooting victim labelled 'subhuman' in online abuse of inquiry witnesses
items.description: Victims of antisemitism have been targeted with death threats and depicted as animals in AI-generated images after giving evidence to the royal commission examining the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket are billion dollar bets banned from Australia — for now
items.description: Kalshi and Polymarket have gone from obscure start-ups to two of the world's biggest prediction markets where users bet on yes-or-no questions spanning politics, pop culture and war.

items.title: Cuba calls US oil blockade 'an act of war' at UN Security Council

featured_image.name: US oil, energy blockade 'is an act of war,' Cuba warns at UN

items.description:
Cuba's Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla addressed the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday, warning that the U.S. oil blockade against his country amounts to an act of war and calling on the international community to mobilize against what he described as an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe.

"The oil and energy siege imposed by the United States against Cuba is, in its effects, equivalent to a naval blockade — an act of war," Rodríguez said, according to a statement posted by Cuba's foreign ministry. He added that "the government of the United States, by its deeds, is in a position to erode international peace and security."[1][2]

"I call on the international community to mobilize to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe that could be imposed through arms or the fuel blockade," he told the council, adding that "now should be the time for solidarity with Cuba."[3]

items.title: UK and Poland to sign defense treaty targeting Russian threats

featured_image.name: Britain and Poland are set to sign a big new security treaty

items.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk are set to sign a defence and security treaty in London on Wednesday, marking the latest in a series of bilateral agreements Britain has struck with European partners to confront what officials describe as escalating hostile threats across the continent.

items.title: UN Security Council condemns drone strike on UAE nuclear plant

featured_image.name: Drone strike sparks fire on perimeter of UAE’s Barakah nuclear power plant

items.description: The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday unanimously condemned the drone attack on the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling it a violation of international law, according to Reuters. The statement came more than a week after a drone struck an electrical generator at the Arab world's only nuclear power facility on May 17, sparking a fire but causing no injuries or radiation release.[1]

items.title: Iran calls U.S. strikes a ceasefire breach as Qatar talks continue
items.description: The U.S. military launched strikes against missile installations and vessels in southern Iran on Monday, targeting sites near Bandar Abbas along the Strait of Hormuz, in a move that drew immediate condemnation from Tehran and threatened to upend fragile peace negotiations taking place simultaneously in Qatar.

items.title: Israel intensifies Lebanon strikes as US-Iran deal nears

featured_image.name: Israel will escalate strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon, Netanyahu says |  Reuters

items.description: Israel is pressing the United States to guarantee its continued freedom to conduct military operations in Lebanon as part of any emerging peace framework with Iran, even as Israeli airstrikes killed multiple people in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley on Tuesday and the country's opposition leader declared the prospective agreement a failure.

items.title: Iran's judiciary blocks presidential order to restore internet

featured_image.name: Iran judiciary suspends presidential body after it ordered internet restored  | The Straits Times

items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the restoration of international internet access on May 25, seeking to end what has become the longest nationwide internet shutdown in history. Internet monitoring group NetBlocks confirmed partial connectivity was restored on Tuesday. But within hours, Iran's judiciary suspended the very presidential body responsible for carrying out the order, plunging the country's digital future into uncertainty.

items.title: BP removes chairman Albert Manifold over conduct concerns
items.description: BP on Tuesday removed Albert Manifold as chairman and director with immediate effect, citing "serious concerns" related to governance standards, oversight, and conduct — a sudden ouster that came just eight months into his tenure atop the British oil giant.[1][2][3]

items.title: President Trump Announces U.S. Military Airstrike in Venezuela
items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].
